 DA hike: Bihar govt increases DA, DR for employees and pensioners ahead of Chhath—Here's all we know
 The Bihar government increased DA and DR for employees and pensioners, effective 1 July 2026, and approved career progression for urban local body staff. Here's all we know about the state Cabinet decisions.
 Written By Jocelyn Fernandes Updated 12 Nov 2026, 07:40 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google The Bihar Cabinet hiked DA and DR for state government employees and pensioners, effective July 1, 2026, under the 5th, 6th and 7th pay commissions. ( AI-generated image used for representational purpose ) AI Quick Read DA hike news: Bihar has hiked Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR) for state government employees and pensioners covered under the 5th, 6th and 7th Central Pay Commissions (CPCs).
 The hike was approved by the Bihar Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, and comes ahead of Chhath Puja festivities in the state, PTI reported.
 Bihar DA, DR hike: What we know
 Bihar on Tuesday approved the enhancement of DA and DR for employees and pensioners, with effect from 1 July 2026. The state finance department, in a notification, said that the Cabinet approved DA and DR as follows:
 Under the 7th Pay Commission structure, DA/DR has been raised by 3%, from 60% to 63%.
 Also Read | 7th Pay Commission: Level 5 govt staff pay rises to ₹62,224 with 63% DA Those covered by the 6th Pay Commission will receive a 7% increase, from 262% to 269%.
 For employees and pensioners under the 5th Pay Commission, the DA/DR rate has been enhanced by 14% from 483% to 497%.
 Revised rates will benefit state government employees, pensioners and family pensioners under the respective pay structures, a senior finance department official told the agency.
 Bihar Cabinet decisions: Key highlights
 — The Cabinet also approved the implementation of the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme for regular employees of urban local bodies in the state.
 Also Read | Top stocks to watch today: Tata Power, Bajaj Finance shares in focus on Thursday — “The decision is aimed at providing financial advancement to employees who often retire after serving for years in the same post without any promotion or career progression opportunities. The move follows long-standing demands from urban local body employees, who lacked provisions for regular promotions,” said the approved proposal of the Urban Development and Housing Department.
 — The government is of the view that the scheme would boost employees' motivation, efficiency and commitment towards discharging their duties and responsibilities, said an official.
 — To encourage innovation, entrepreneurship and startup culture among female students studying in higher educational institutions, and to develop their innovative ideas into practical business ventures, the Cabinet approved the launch of the ‘Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme’ (Bihar's Daughter Startup Challenge Scheme).
 — “The scheme will benefit a maximum of 2,100 female students , starting from the current financial year. It will remain in operation for four financial years, from FY27 to FY30. Administrative approval of ₹ 88.20 crore has been granted for the implementation of the scheme”, said the approved proposal of the Higher Education Department.
 Also Read | Weather today: IMD issues rain alert; Delhi to see shallow fog today Also Read | Nvidia preparing to oust Jensen Huang after second affair with employee — In an attempt to encourage the participation of female students in higher education and research, the Cabinet approved the launch of the ‘Mukhyamantri Balika PhD Fellowship Scheme’.
 — To remain in operation for four financial years from FY27 to FY30, the approved proposal of the Department of Youth, Employment and Skill Development is expected to increase the overall enrolment ratio of women in higher education and enable female students to benefit from higher education.
 Bihar Artificial Intelligence Mission
 The Cabinet also approved the Department of Information Technology's proposal to establish the 'Bihar Artificial Intelligence Mission' to position Bihar as a leading state in AI.
 "One of its main objectives is to identify leading industries and institutions in the AI sector and secure their participation to develop an AI ecosystem within the state. To achieve this objective, M/s Global Finance and Technology Network (GFTN), Singapore, has been selected based on its nomination to strengthen the state's Artificial Intelligence ecosystem, skill development and innovation", said the approved proposal.
 With the support of GFTN, the National University of Singapore -Asian Institute of Digital Finance (NUS-AIDF) and Lynx Foundation, an advanced five-month AI certification programme will be conducted.
 At least 7,000 students (STEM/Non-STEM, undergraduate/postgraduate) will be trained over five years.
 Through GFTN, an AI- and Quantum-enabled Digital Sandbox platform (Aryabhata Technology Observatory) will be established, said an official.
 To address Bihar's specific challenges, startups, entrepreneurs, students, researchers and government officials will be provided with AI/ML APIs, Data Pipelines, an LLM Gateway and a Cloud IDE, he added.
 "Bihar will be presented before global investors, technology companies and policymakers through 12 global platforms of GFTN, including the Singapore FinTech Festival, Point Zero Forum Zurich , Black Swan Summit, Bangkok Digital Finance Forum and GFTN Forum Japan," the official added.
 (With inputs from PTI)
